'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.trans: Ninul, plug in the soldering iron.

examples.text: Он всегда включает свет на кухне.
examples.trans: He always switches on the kitchen light.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you

to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

examples.text: Мама говорила, что у меня на икру аллергия.
examples.trans: Mum said I'm allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: as a reply on its own

examples.trans: I didn't understand a thing, Arkash.

плевать.gloss: not to care, couldn't care less (+ dative)

meanings.en: couldn't care less, don't care (colloquial predicative: мне плевать на + accusative)

examples.text: Если тебе плевать на дочь, то мне нет!
examples.trans: If you don't care about our daughter, I do!
My parents don't care about me.

examples.trans: Buy half a kilo of cheese.
And the half-kilo of expensive caviar?

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'анный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('devoted, loyal').

examples.trans: I am devoted to the chef.
My friends are loyal to me.

examples.text: Мои люди преданы мне до конца.
examples.trans: My people are loyal to me to the end.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'device, apparatus' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do not turn on the device!
Chef, please do not turn on the device!

examples.text: Шеф, мы уже выключили все шумные приборы.
examples.trans: Chef, we have already turned off all noisy equipment.

meanings.note: ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)
